![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/9d8f2d52a0d943a4eeb1d323cc90db145c9b87b57e87d595a7ca5809498e7a6a.png)

Consider the region bounded by the curve $x=y+1,$ the vertical line $x=4,$ and the horizontal line $y=0,$ as shown in the picture. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=4.$

$V=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersection of the curve and the line $x=4$ by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y+1 & =4 \\ y & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the limits of integration are from $y=0$ to $y=3$ along the $y$-axis.

To determine which is the left and which is the right function, let's draw our horizontal arrow.  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/f9fd1773b9599b1a4b61fc58c854bf998ed147a9707f719a80a3588874c0eb4f.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=y+1,$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=4.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}[(\text{right function})-(\text{left function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}[4-(y+1)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}(3-y)^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3}(3-y)^{3}\,{|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3}(0-{3}^{3}) \\  & =9\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
